lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Ezra: overview
nodes.d: Ezra reports the return from Babylon under Cyrus and Zerubbabel and the rebuilding of the temple despite opposition (chs. 1-6), then Ezra's own journey to Jerusalem, his prayer over intermarriage, and the people's covenant to put away foreign wives (chs. 7-10).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Ezra, from Cyrus's decree to the people's confession?
ev: Name the two parts: the return and temple under Zerubbabel, and Ezra's mission
Say how the book begins (Cyrus) and ends (the list of those with foreign wives)

nodes.t: Cyrus's decree and the first return
nodes.d: In the first year of Cyrus the LORD stirs his spirit, and he proclaims that the LORD God of heaven charged him to build a house in Jerusalem and invites any of God's people to go up. Those whose spirit God raised go, neighbours help them, and Cyrus brings out the temple vessels to Sheshbazzar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Cyrus decreed and who went up to Jerusalem?
ev: Say whose word was being fulfilled (1:1)
Say what Cyrus returned to Sheshbazzar (1:7-11)

nodes.t: The list of those who returned
nodes.d: Chapter 2 lists those who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua by family and town, then priests, Levites, singers, porters and temple servants, notes some who could not prove their ancestry, and gives the total and the freewill gifts for the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Ezra records the names and numbers of the returnees?
ev: Say who led the group (2:2)
Say what some of the chief fathers gave (2:68-69)

nodes.t: The altar is rebuilt and worship begins
nodes.d: In the seventh month the people gather at Jerusalem; Jeshua and Zerubbabel build the altar of the God of Israel, offer burnt offerings morning and evening as written in the law of Moses, and keep the feast of tabernacles, although fear was on them because of the people of the lands.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the returned exiles began by building the altar?
ev: Say what they built first and why (3:2-3)
Name the feast they kept (3:4)

nodes.t: The foundation of the temple is laid
nodes.d: In the second year the builders lay the foundation, with priests and Levites praising the LORD according to David's order; the people shout for joy, while many old men who had seen the first house weep, so that joy and weeping cannot be told apart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why some people shouted for joy and some wept when the foundation was laid?
ev: Describe what the people sang (3:11)
Say why some of the old men wept (3:12)

nodes.t: The adversaries offer to help and then oppose
nodes.d: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin ask to build with Zerubbabel, claiming they seek his God; Zerubbabel and Jeshua refuse, saying they must build alone as Cyrus commanded, and the people of the land weaken their hands and hire counsellors against them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Zerubbabel refused the offer to help build the temple?
ev: Say what the adversaries asked and what the leaders answered (4:2-3)
Say how they opposed the work (4:4-5)

nodes.t: Letters to the king and the work stops
nodes.d: Later accusations are written against Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes; Rehum and Shimshai write to Artaxerxes that Jerusalem is a rebellious city, and the king orders the work stopped. The work on the house of God ceases until the second year of Darius.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the rebuilding was stopped and for how long?
ev: Say what the letter claimed about Jerusalem (4:12-16)
Say how long the work ceased (4:24)

nodes.t: Haggai and Zechariah and the resumed work
nodes.d: Haggai and Zechariah prophesy to the Jews in the name of the God of Israel, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua rise and begin to build again; when Tatnai the governor asks who commanded it, the text says the eye of their God was on the elders.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who encouraged the Jews to start building again?
ev: Name the prophets and the leaders who began again (5:1-2)
Say what kept the work going when Tatnai questioned them (5:5)

nodes.t: Tatnai writes to Darius
nodes.d: Tatnai and his companions write to Darius reporting that the Jews are building the house of the great God, say they build as servants of the God of heaven and earth by Cyrus's decree, and ask the king to search the records.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the Jewish elders told Tatnai about Cyrus's decree?
ev: Say what the elders said about who commanded the building (5:11-16)
Say what Tatnai asked Darius to do (5:17)

nodes.t: Darius finds Cyrus's decree
nodes.d: A search in the house of the rolls finds Cyrus's decree about the house of God in Jerusalem; Darius orders Tatnai to let the work alone, give costs from the royal revenue, supply offerings, and punish anyone who changes the decree.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the opposition to building the temple was ended?
ev: Say where the decree of Cyrus was found (6:1-2)
State what Darius commanded (6:6-12)

nodes.t: The temple is finished and dedicated
nodes.d: Tatnai carries out the decree, and the elders of the Jews build and prosper through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah; the house is finished on the third of Adar in Darius's sixth year, dedicated with joy, and the Passover is kept.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the second temple was completed and celebrated?
ev: Say when the house was finished (6:15)
Say what they kept after the dedication (6:19-22)

nodes.t: Ezra the scribe goes up to Jerusalem
nodes.d: In the reign of Artaxerxes, Ezra, a priest of the line of Aaron and a ready scribe in the law of Moses, goes up from Babylon with a company because the good hand of God was on him; the text says he prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, to do it, and to teach in Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who Ezra was and why he went to Jerusalem?
ev: Say what Ezra had prepared his heart to do (7:10)
Say what is said about the hand of God on him (7:6, 9)

nodes.t: Artaxerxes' letter and Ezra's blessing
nodes.d: Artaxerxes' letter lets Ezra take volunteers, silver and gold and vessels to Jerusalem, orders treasurers to supply him, and tells Ezra to appoint judges to teach and enforce the law of God. Ezra blesses the LORD who put this in the king's heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the king's letter gave Ezra and how Ezra responded?
ev: Say what the king authorised Ezra to do (7:13-26)
Say how Ezra responded (7:27-28)

nodes.t: The family heads who went up with Ezra
nodes.d: Ezra 8:1-14 lists the chief fathers and the number of men who went up with Ezra in the reign of Artaxerxes, by family.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Ezra 8:1-14 records?
ev: Say what the list records
Name at least one family that went up

nodes.t: Fasting at the river Ahava
nodes.d: At the river Ahava Ezra finds no Levites and sends for some; he proclaims a fast to seek a right way, being ashamed to ask the king for soldiers after saying God's hand is for good on those who seek him. They entrust the silver, gold and vessels to twelve priests, travel safely, and deliver the treasure in Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Ezra fasted instead of asking for an escort?
ev: Say why Ezra did not ask for soldiers (8:22)
Say how God answered the fast (8:23, 31)

nodes.t: Intermarriage reported to Ezra
nodes.d: The princes tell Ezra that the people, priests and Levites have not separated from the peoples of the lands and have taken their daughters as wives, the princes and rulers being chief in this trespass; Ezra tears his garment and hair and sits appalled.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the people had done that grieved Ezra?
ev: Say what the princes reported (9:1-2)
Say how Ezra reacted (9:3)

nodes.t: Ezra's confession
nodes.d: At the evening sacrifice Ezra falls on his knees and confesses the people's guilt from their fathers' days, remembers the mercy shown in giving a remnant and a little reviving, and says they have again broken God's commandments, and that the LORD is righteous.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise how Ezra prayed over the people's sin?
ev: Say what mercy Ezra recalls (9:8-9)
Say how Ezra ends the prayer (9:15)

nodes.t: The people covenant to put away foreign wives
nodes.d: As Ezra weeps before the house of God a great congregation weeps with him; Shechaniah says there is hope in Israel and proposes making a covenant to put away the foreign wives according to the law. Ezra has the leaders swear and a gathering is held in Jerusalem, where the people confess and agree to separate.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the people agreed to do after Ezra's prayer?
ev: Say what Shechaniah proposed (10:2-4)
Say how the matter was carried out (10:7-17)

nodes.t: The names of those with foreign wives
nodes.d: Ezra 10:18-44 lists priests, Levites, singers, porters and other Israelites who had taken foreign wives, with a ram of the flock as guilt offering from the priests, and ends by noting that some had children by these wives.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Ezra 10:18-44 records and how the book closes?
ev: Say what the priests offered (10:19)
Say how the book of Ezra ends (10:44)

nodes.t: 2 Chronicles: overview
nodes.d: 2 Chronicles tells of Solomon's wisdom and the temple (chs. 1-9), then the kings of Judah from Rehoboam to Zedekiah, with attention to temple worship, reform and returning to the LORD, ending with the exile and Cyrus's decree to rebuild the house (ch. 36).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Chronicles in order, from Solomon's temple to Cyrus's decree?
ev: Say that the book follows Solomon's temple and then the kings of Judah
Say how it ends (36:22-23, Cyrus of Persia)

nodes.t: Cyrus's decree
nodes.d: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia the LORD stirs up his spirit to proclaim that the LORD God of heaven has charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and invites any of his people to go up.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how 2 Chronicles closes and what Cyrus announced?
ev: Say whose spirit the LORD stirred up and what he proclaimed
Say how 2 Chronicles ends

nodes.t: Nehemiah: overview
nodes.d: Nehemiah, cupbearer to Artaxerxes, prays and returns to Jerusalem to rebuild its wall in fifty-two days despite opposition (chs. 1-7), then the law is read, the feast of booths is kept, the people confess and covenant (chs. 8-10), and the city is repopulated, the wall dedicated and abuses corrected (chs. 11-13).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Nehemiah, from the prayer in Susa to the reforms at the end?
ev: Name the main parts: building the wall, reading the law and covenant, dedication and reforms
Say who Nehemiah was and what he did for Jerusalem

nodes.t: Guarding Jerusalem and the register of the first returnees
nodes.d: With the wall built and doors set up, Nehemiah puts Hanani and Hananiah in charge of Jerusalem and sets watches at the gates; the city is large but its people few, so God puts it in Nehemiah's heart to gather the people by genealogy, and he finds the register of those who came up first, which is read out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Nehemiah looked for the register of the first returnees?
ev: Say who was put in charge and how the gates were guarded (7:1-3)
Say what record Nehemiah found (7:5)
